quizzes.stem: Scenario: Dana runs the refund flow of a claims assistant. The service that screens incoming requests stops answering, and the code must choose between two behaviours for a request that asks for a refund. Which one fits the design rules on this page?

options.a: Hold it and tell the caller that the check is unavailable
options.b: Let the request pass and flag it for a person to look at tomorrow
options.c: Run the request once more through the model's own safety training
options.d: Let the request pass because the later approval step will catch it

explanation.a: A refund is a high-consequence action and the screen is an input control, so the design holds.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A screen that is down and lets a request through is the opening an attacker waits for".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the layers "answer different attackers and different mistakes", and the model's own training is not the missing screen.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "an output control cannot stop a tool call that already happened", and a later step does not repair a gap on an earlier layer.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Ravi reviews a design in which a model must "always ask a person before closing an account", a rule written in the system prompt. What is the main weakness of that design?

options.a: The sentence is too short for the model to follow it reliably under load
options.b: The rule should sit in the user turn so that the model reads it last
options.c: Nothing forces the step to happen, because an instruction only asks
options.d: The sentence repeats a rule the platform already applies to every account

explanation.c: A line in a prompt is a request and a control is a step the model cannot skip.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page does not argue about length: "a line in a prompt is a request, and a control is a step the model cannot skip".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the sentence stays "a request to the model and not a control" wherever it sits.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Every control has a failure mode of its own, and the design must say it", and no platform rule is assumed to hold it.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Mira is asked to honour a deletion request from a customer whose requests appear in the audit entries of a claims assistant. Those entries hold tokens, and one table maps each token to a person. What does the design do?

options.a: Delete the entries of that customer from the log
options.b: Remove the vault rows that tie them to anything in the log
options.c: Replace the tokens in that customer's entries with new tokens
options.d: Encrypt that customer's entries with a key that is then kept

explanation.b: Removing the vault rows leaves the entries and unlinks them from the person.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Deleting every audit entry would destroy the proof".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "keeping both leaves the person identifiable", and new tokens in the entries leave the vault map in place.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the design removes "the map: the vault entries for that person go", and encryption keeps a key that can link them again.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Tomas must set how long a support assistant keeps its audit records. His design has a shortest period, a longest period and a number of days between them. A court order then opens a case that covers a set of those records. What happens to those records?

options.a: They are deleted at once because the court may inspect any copy
options.b: They follow the same schedule and the case uses what is left
options.c: They are moved to a table with no limit on their retention
options.d: Hold them past the ceiling until the matter is settled

explanation.d: A legal hold is the one thing that outranks the ceiling, and the records are released when it ends.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the hold keeps records, as "the records in scope are kept past it".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "they are released when the hold ends", and an unlimited table keeps them after the case.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A legal hold is the one thing that outranks the ceiling", so the ordinary schedule does not apply.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Ines's claims assistant keeps its record of each request for a year, and a reviewer notices that the screen that checks incoming requests is allowed to let them through when it is down. Which change does the first page support?

options.a: Keep the pass-through and add a monitor that alerts on the gap
options.b: Keep the pass-through and shorten the retention of the records
options.c: Stop the call whenever that service cannot answer, and log why
options.d: Move the screening into the system prompt so that it cannot be down

explanation.c: An input control holds when it fails, and the reason goes in the record.
explanation.b: Ruled out because retention does not close the gap: "A screen that is down and lets a request through is the opening an attacker waits for".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the first page puts the monitor in the layers that watch "afterwards", so "an output control cannot stop a tool call that already happened".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a line in a prompt is a request, and a control is a step the model cannot skip".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: A review finds that a model system's average accuracy is 94 percent, and that one language group, a small part of the traffic, scores 70 percent. The team says the system passes. What does the second page say about that claim?

options.a: A small group cannot be measured, so the average is the only usable figure
options.b: Fairness is a gap between segments, and a headline figure masks a failing one
options.c: The group's score should be dropped when it is below the volume needed
options.d: The system passes because the model was tested on a broad set before launch

explanation.b: The page measures fairness as a gap per group and warns that an average hides one.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "the groups must be defined where they can be measured" and a group that can be labelled can be reported.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a headline average hides a failing group exactly as it hides a failing segment", so dropping the score hides it.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "fairness is a property of outcomes by group", and a broad launch test is not a gap measure.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: An auditor asks a team to prove that a refund over a set amount was approved by a person. The team has an audit entry for the refund with a request id, an outcome of human and a character count. What do they have?

options.a: Nothing, because a record without the content is not admissible
options.b: A record that is too thin, since only the text proves what happened
options.c: A record that holds the refund amount and the approver's name
options.d: Proof of the step, with no copy of the customer's text kept

explanation.d: The record shows the step happened without a copy of the data.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Content that was never stored cannot be breached, subpoenaed by accident or kept past a deletion request".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the entry holds "request id, action, consequence, outcome and the size of the text", which names no amount or approver.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the design keeps "proof of what happened", and the page does not tie proof to stored content.
